message.reasoning:
The finding: PluginBot tool typosquatting via register_tool. Attacker registers lookalike tool name; server accepts; registered tool has no handler, so as implemented it just shows in tools/list. As documented, malicious tool runs in place of legitimate one.

CVSS: AV:N (MCP port, though loopback by default... network), AC:L, AT:N, PR:N, UI:N? "As documented, later caller selects lookalike name" — UI could be A/active? The caller must make a typo — no user interaction exactly; UI:N. Impact: VC? Tool registry poisoning — partial impact on the registry. As implemented, lookalike entry with no handler; low impact. VC:L? VI:N, VA:N... Downstream: if malicious tool executes in place of legitimate — could exfiltrate etc. Score default config as documented? "Score the lab default configuration as documented." Default config: no LLM, tools advertised only, no handler → impact is a poisoned tool list entry. But documented behavior is substitution. I'd say VC:L/VI:L/VA:N, SC:N SI:N SA:N? Substitution could leak secrets via store_secret... but no handler exists. Keep VI:N, SC:N etc. Actually a lookalike entry could cause callers to send args to it—no handler means failure. Low impact.

Vector: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:L/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N

AIVSS:
- LC: entry is JSON-RPC tools/call naming register_tool — attacker-supplied tool name influences tool invocation path. Not natural language? It's direct attacker input reaching tool registry without mediation. LC D? LC concerns natural language; here tool name string is structured but direct. I'd say D (direct attacker-controlled input reaching privileged tool path).
- CP: registered tool persists in the tool registry across requests within server process — session context? Registry persists across requests/callers, in-process, lost at restart. That's like memory: durable within process. Rubric C requires durable stores/vector DB etc.; S is ephemeral session. Registry persists beyond a single session but not durable store... S fits best ("ephemeral session state, session-scoped cache, unreachable after session boundary" — it's reachable across sessions though). Hmm. Registration persists across requests indefinitely within process. Could argue C (durable store — tool registry alters standing behaviour/tool list). I'll pick C: persists and alters advertised tool list, remains after originating session ends. That fits "standing behaviour" alteration.
- AP: effect confined to PluginBot's tool registry → N? Or C: influence relays to callers who select the lookalike tool. As implemented, no handler → N. As documented, callers (agents/users) select it — relay to another component. Default: the entry appears in tools/list and has no handler → contained? No propagation. I'll pick N (confined to PluginBot registry).
- RH: no evaluator/reward channels involved → N? RH D requires verified reward hacking; N requires test confirming isolation. No proxy objectives on this path. I'd say N? Actually RH N: "every evaluator... sits outside agent's reach... test confirms isolation." There's no evaluator at all in this path; N with high confidence? Or X. I'll pick N, reachable_proxy false, isolation_verified true (no proxy channels on path, automated test confirms only a registry entry).
- ES: PluginBot accepts tool registrations at run time with no signature/source check → W (wide: dynamic tool registration unvetted).

Automatable: Yes (curl command, automated test).
Technical impact: Partial (registry poisoning, no handler in default).
Applicability as implemented: model_directed_goal_pursuit false (no model called in default), selects_or_sequences_actions false.
As modeled: PluginBot is a tool server, not model — false as well; agent doesn't pursue goals via model.

rh_facts: reachable_proxy false, isolation_verified true, verified_episodes 0, episodes_reviewed 0(?), locus "PluginBot tool registry (port 7012)".
